Fixer · UI handoff

What this file is

The approved UI direction for Fixer, a free Lightroom Classic alternative written in Rust. It holds every mockup screen (rendered to static HTML), the design system they share, and the full feature inventory with priorities. It is the starting brief for implementation.

For Claude Code

How to read the mocks

  • Every screen is 1440 × 900 and built from the same shell: top bar 44 px, main row 714 px (left panel 252 px, center, right panel 304 px), filmstrip 90 px, status bar 22 px, 6 px outer padding and 6 px gaps.
  • The photo is a placeholder SVG scene. Real images replace it.
  • Numbers, names and EXIF values are sample data.
  • Screens are static. Hover, open and active states are shown as frozen examples.
  • Use "Open full size" on any screen to inspect it with browser dev tools.

What to build from it

  • Port the tokens and component styles in Design system into CSS variables and Svelte 5 components. The frontend is Tauri 2 with Svelte 5 and TypeScript, as decided in the technical spec. Treat this file as the visual target, not as code to reuse.
  • Build the shared components first (the Components group in Screens). Every screen is composed from them.
  • Implement features in the milestone order of the technical spec (M0 to M5), as laid out in docs/development-plan.md. Priority (P0, P1, P2) says what is in v1, not the build order. Each feature in the Features tab lists its screens and open questions.
  • Where this file and the technical spec disagree, the spec wins.
  • The feature list is also delivered as FEATURES.md, where specs will be written per feature.

Product decisions

Direction

  • Layout follows Lightroom Classic. Only the look changes.
  • Style "Carbon Glass": dense, keyboard-first, flat #121212 background everywhere, glass only on interactive details.
  • Module bar: Library, Develop, Export. Map and Print join it after v1, when those modules ship. Book, Slideshow and Web are deferred.

AI policy

  • No generative AI. Nothing in the app creates new pixels.
  • AI may assist selection and masking (subject, sky, background, objects, people; face grouping after v1) and restoration (AI denoise). Models run on device.
  • Remove ships as heal and clone, with AI object detection to help select. Content-aware fill from nearby pixels and super resolution come after v1.

Menus and commands

  • No classic menu bar. Full menu behind the logo button (also Alt).
  • Most used commands are one-click quick actions in the top bar, per module, customizable and pinnable from any right-click menu.
  • Ctrl K searches commands, presets, photos and collections.

Performance rule

  • Real backdrop blur only on slider handles and selection indicators. Elements floating over the photo (photo toolbar, badges, overlays) use a flat, near-opaque fill.
  • Panels and selection states are gradients and borders only, so they are cheap to draw.

Surfaces

Pane (flat)

Every panel. No blur.

background: #121212;
border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.07);
border-radius: 12px;

Lens (selection)

Active module, tool, preset, segmented choice, hovered menu item, primary buttons. No blur.

background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.16), rgba(255,255,255,0.07));
border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.32), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.25);
color: #ffffff;

Overlay (over the photo)

Photo toolbar, badges, small overlays and photo-anchored dialogs. Flat, no backdrop blur (technical spec). The screens still render these with blur; build the flat version below.

background: rgba(22,23,30,0.92);
border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.16);
box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0.5px rgba(255,255,255,0.45), 0 12px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.35);

Slider

Track 3 px, fill flat accent (no glow), handle a glossy near-opaque capsule 18 × 13.

track: rgba(255,255,255,0.12)   /* or a color gradient for Temp, Tint, HSL */
fill: #5b9dff from center (bipolar) or from left
handle: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.95), rgba(220,222,228,.82));
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.6);
  box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 #fff, inset 0 -1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.18), 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.5);
label/value: text.strong when changed, text.muted / text.dim at default

Rules

  • Glass means you can grab or select it. Flat means information.
  • Edited state is always visible: blue dot on edited panels, bright label and value on changed sliders, dot on edited thumbnails.
  • Every command shows its shortcut where it appears (menus, tooltips, quick actions, search results).
  • Right-click menus act on the whole selection and show mixed states with "–".
  • Dialogs size to the window (min(target, 100% - 48px)) and their content wraps or scrolls instead of overflowing.
